questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: First and foremost, I looked at the courses available at the study destination. It was very important to me that the destination provided some interesting and relevant courses. Furthermore, I also wanted to go somewhere with a rich cultural and literary history, where I would be able to got o a lot of museums and do other cultural activities.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Overall my exchange experience was amazing, however, there was some administrative issues which made the experience a bit stressful especially in the beginning, as I felt like I did not have enough information.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I found it quite hard. There was an office for international students where I could go and get some guidance, but there was a lot of information which I would have preferred to have before my arrival. This, for example, includes knowing exactly what courses I was going to attend, and when they would begin.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I went to the office, and they did help somewhat.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I found it quite hard to find housing off campus. I would have preferred to live on campus, however, I only became aware of the housing opportunities on campus when it was already too late. It would have been great if the different campus housing options had been mentioned at the orientation day in Copenhagen.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: They should be aware that living off campus is quite expensive, and you won't necessarily live with other students. If you want to live off campus, I would recommend to begin the search for apartments early, but in general I would not recommend living off campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I found it fairly easy to register for the courses, but the process of finding eligible courses was quite hard and complicated.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The registration process was quite easy, but finding courses was hard because a lot of the course's information came late, and furthermore, there was a lot of courses that did not end up being created, so it was hard to tell which courses you could actually take in the given semester.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Again you could go to the office for international students, however, it was very limited what they could help with in regard to choosing courses.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was very successful, as I ended up registering for all the classes that I wanted to attend.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: To be patient, as the process of finding courses and making a schedule  where they all fit together can be long, but in the end you will figure it out.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level depended on the specific course, but in general I would say that the level of the courses was average.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: In Copenhagen I am used to a mixture of lectures, group-work and student participation, however, in Milan it was almost exclusively lecture. I found this quite strange, as I believe that group-work and student participation are greats ways to learn.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Globalization, Social Justice and Human Rights (6)
Journalism, Media and Politics (6)
Contemporary English Literature (9)
Human Development and Mobility in a Changing World (9)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend Contemporary English Literature and Human Development and Mobility in a Changing World, because I found both of these courses extremely interesting, and moreover, the professors were very dedicated to their subjects.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I had to buy some kitchen equipment, which was unexpected.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The housing was a lot more expensive then what I expected. However, the transportation was cheaper than what i am used to in Copenhagen.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: ESN created a lot of different bot cultural, athletic and social activities which you could participate in and where you could meet a lot of other exchange students.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend participating in some of the ESN events. Particularly, I liked a pasta-making course and to visit nearby cities.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I would recommend that they go on trips to the nearby cities such as Verona, Venice, Lake Como etc. These cities are all fairly easy to reach by train and bus, and they are all very beautiful and cultural interesting places.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I found it quite easy, as the difference between Italian culture and Danish culture isn't too shocking. Of course there are some major differences, but personally I think it's exciting to get to experience and learn about other cultures.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I think the easiest way is to talk to the local students during classes. You can either before or after a class approach them and talk to them about the course.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: It seems to me that Italy may have a more laid-back approach to academics then what I am used to in Denmark - for example in Milan I didn't really get a study plan for any of my courses, which for me was quite challenging as I like to have an overview of the reading material.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I love Italian art, so I very much enjoyed visiting a lot of museums and such. Also the food is very lovely and especially Aperitivo is a quite nice concept.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: To be patient, keep your mind open, and maybe make sure to have some savings beforehand, as going on exchange can be quite expensive, especially if you want to go on a lot of weekend trips and such.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I was unaware that the oral exams would be so different from what I am used to in Copenhagen. All my oral exams in Milan was in held in a big room where all the students arrive at the same time, and then you do the exam one by one in front of everyone. For me, this was quite strange and uncomfortable, so I think it's worth being aware of it beforehand.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting people from so many different cultures and countries and hearing about their lives etc. Furthermore, I got to visit a lot of beautiful cities in the weekends, which was also full of great experiences.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: For me, finding housing was the greatest challenge.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
